requirement_text: "Ankara University will admit international students into its associate and undergraduate programs based on the TR-YÖS Exam and equivalent exam results (such as the International Baccalaureate Diploma, Germany ABITUR, TQDK (DIM), GCE (A LEVEL), SAT etc.)" "Only one examination result is to be used for the application... Applications with multiple examination results will not be evaluated." General (non-elevated-threshold) minimum scores by exam, per the official valid-exams table: TR-YÖS minimum 200 points (valid 2 years from exam date); Germany ABITUR minimum 4 points; International Baccalaureate (IB) minimum 30 points; GCE (A LEVEL) and Cambridge International AL/ASL minimum 320 points, "Level 2A, with at least an A grade in one subject related to the applied programme"; TQDK/DİM minimum 400 out of 700, in a field related to the applied programme; WASSCE-WAEC B2-level scores in six subjects, at least one related to the applied programme; SAT minimum 1100 total and minimum 650 in Math (Math score used for evaluation/placement, valid 2 years from exam date -- the 2026-1 cycle announcement further specifies this as "SAT results belonging ONLY to the dates between 2024 June and 2026 June"); Kyrgyzstan ORT minimum 200 out of 250; General High School Diploma with graduation GPA of at least 80/100 (excluding diplomas from schools located in Türkiye) used only to fill quotas remaining vacant after exam-based placement.
scope: all programmes except the elevated-threshold list in ANK0002
researcher_notes: This is genuinely a two-tier system, not one flat exam-acceptance table -- see ANK0002 for the higher, programme-specific TR-YÖS-only thresholds that apply instead of this general table for a named set of competitive programmes (Medicine, Dentistry, Computer Engineering, Law, etc). Extracted from the official PDF via pypdf after the wrapping HTML pages (isoidb.ankara.edu.tr, iso.ankara.edu.tr) served only navigation shells with the actual score table embedded as a linked PDF -- direct WebFetch/curl of the HTML pages could not surface this content, the PDF had to be located (via its href in the raw HTML) and fetched/parsed directly.

requirement_text: Elevated TR-YÖS-only minimum-score tiers for named competitive programmes, per the official valid-exams table (equivalent exams from ANK0001 are NOT accepted for these programmes -- TR-YÖS only): "Minimum 440 points from TR-YÖS" for Medicine, Medicine (English), Dentistry, Dentistry (English), Computer Engineering, Computer Engineering (English), Electrical-Electronics Engineering (English), Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering, Software Engineering. "Minimum 400 points from TR-YÖS" for Pharmacy, Pharmacy (English), Biomedical Engineering (English). "Minimum 300 points from TR-YÖS" for Civil Engineering, Nursing, Midwifery. "Minimum 275 points from TR-YÖS" for Law, Law (English), Veterinary, Veterinary (English), Physics Engineering (English), Food Engineering (English), Geophysical Engineering (English), Geological Engineering (English), Chemical Engineering (English).
scope: named programmes only (see requirement_text) -- program-level fact, no program_id link attempted this pass since these are department/programme names, not this corpus's canonical program_id
limitations: The source table doesn't state explicitly whether IB/A-Level/SAT/etc are entirely inadmissible for these named programmes or simply unlisted (no equivalent-exam score given) -- read as TR-YÖS-only by the table's own structure (a single 'Required Score' column per programme group, no other exam type listed for these rows), but this exact exclusivity was not independently confirmed via a second official source this pass.
researcher_notes: This is a real, structurally distinct requirement from ANK0001 -- program-specific and elevated, not a variant of the general table. If ingested, this should NOT collapse into ANK0001's TR-YÖS=200 threshold for these specific programmes.

requirement_text: "Although the primary language of instruction at our University is Turkish, certain programs are conducted entirely in a foreign language." "Candidates from abroad are required to prove their Turkish proficiency level with a Turkish Language Proficiency Certificate from Ankara University Turkish and Foreign Languages Research and Application Center (TÖMER) or Yunus Emre Institute. Those who cannot provide this document will be given a maximum of 2 years to prove their Turkish proficiency. Candidates who fail to prove their Turkish proficiency within this period will have their relationship with the University terminated." Exemption: "Candidates who have graduated from secondary education institutions affiliated with the Ministry of National Education (MEB) in Turkey or abroad, those who have graduated from KKTC... high schools and are citizens of KKTC, and those who have graduated from KKTC high schools and are citizens of the Republic of Turkey are exempt from these requirements when applying to programs where courses are taught solely in a specific foreign language."
scope: applies regardless of a programme's own language of instruction; the stated exemption is specifically for MEB/KKTC-schooled applicants applying to fully-foreign-language-taught programmes
researcher_notes: A Turkish-proficiency requirement even for English-medium programmes is a genuinely distinctive fact (not the case at most of this corpus's other institutions) -- worth surfacing to counselor-facing content specifically, not just the raw requirement record, since a student targeting one of Ankara's '(English)' programmes could easily assume no Turkish is needed.
